audit_notes: Model: near-wall settlement with time-split effective attachment: idle periods (fraction f_idle, no shear, thermal switching every t_s removes a fraction p of unconsolidated cells) and service periods (survival s_flow under shear, no switching). k_eff = k_c*[f_idle/(1+p*t_c/t_s) + (1-f_idle)*s_flow]. Design: 1e-4*(0.25/2 + 0.75*0.435) = 4.51e-5 m/s, Da = 0.226, J = 3.68e4 1/(m^2 s). Baseline silicone foul-release without switching (p = 0): 5.76e-5 m/s, Da = 0.288, J = 4.47e4 1/(m^2 s). Expected gain ~18 %, much smaller than the parent's 49 % because switching now happens only during idle periods. The linear flux model underweights idle-period fouling, which consolidates and is not shed later at speed; this is noted but not modelled. Energy check: induction penetration in steel at ~20 kHz is ~0.1-0.2 mm; heating 0.2 mm of steel plus ~0.2 mm of coating by 15 K takes ~3.6e6*2e-4*15 + 1.5e6*2e-4*15 = 11 + 4.5 kJ/m^2, plus losses to water (h ~300 W/m^2K, 2 s) ~9 kJ/m^2 and conduction into the plate: ~20-30 kJ/m^2 per pass. Two passes per day over 10,000 m^2: ~0.5 GJ/day, ~6 kW average during idle; peak power of a 1 m wide head at 0.2 m/s: 0.2 m^2/s*25 kJ/m^2 = 5 kW. Feasible for a battery robot with charging. Heat must pass the 200 um coating within the dwell time: diffusion time (2e-4)^2/1e-7 = 0.4 s, fine. Caveats: p = 0.5 and t_c = 1 day are assumed; brush ageing not modelled. Dimensionless: Da 0.226 (design), 0.288 (baseline); p*t_c/t_s = 1.0. Simulation coefficient: design k_eff 4.51e-5 m/s (informational).
